Title: Buttonhole List Window
Content: It is possible to create, copy, apply and set a style in Buttonhole list window. Without any extra setting, the Default Buttonhole is applied as default. Once the Default Buttonhole style is modified, it lasts until rerun of the program and it is unable to be deleted.

Title: Reset Buttonhole Style Property
Content: Objective Reset buttonhole item properties to default value (ver2.5.0). Location Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Right-Click Buttonhole Item Pop-Up Menu Reset Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Right-Click Buttonhole Item Pop-Up Menu Reset The buttonhole item properties are now being reset back to default value.

Title: Delete Buttonhole Style
Content: Objective Delete unnecessary buttonhole styles. Location Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Select a buttonhole style to be deleted. Press the Delete key on keyboard or right click on the buttonhole style and select Delete. The selected buttonhole style is deleted.

Title: Create 2D Buttonhole Measurement
Content: Objective View buttonhole position from the pattern outline with 2D measurements (ver2.5.0). Location Object Browser Buttonhole Property Editor 2D Measurements To Center Operation Select a buttonhole with Select/Move Button tool in the 3D toolbar. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Buttonhole Property Editor 2D Measurements To Center Select the desired 2D measurement options of the Left/Right/Up/Down. The 2D measurement is now being displayed or hidden accordingly.

Title: Create Additional Buttonhole Style
Content: Objective Create a new buttonhole style. Location Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Add Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Buttonhole Tab Add A new item named after 'Buttonhole 1, 2' is now being created and applied.

Title: Move Fastened Button/Buttonhole
Content: Objective Move a fastened button only, or a button and buttonhole together. Location Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Operation Move Fastened Button Only Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Click and drag the desired button in the 2D or 3D window. The selected button is moved to where the mouse is released. The moved button stays fastened. Move Fastened Button and Buttonhole Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Hold down Shift on the keyboard, then click all buttons and buttonholes to be moved in the 2D or 3D window. Click and drag the selected buttons and buttonholes. The selected buttons and buttonholes are moved to where the mouse is released. The moved buttons and buttonholes stay fastened.

Title: BUTTON STYLE PROPERTIES: Button Name
Content: Objective Rename buttons as desired. Location Object Browser Button Tab Property Editor Change Name Operation Object Browser Select a button item in the Button Tab. Its properties appear in the Property Editor. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor Name Change Name The name is now being edited and applied.

Title: BUTTON STYLE PROPERTIES: Button Shape
Content: Objective Change button shapes as desired. Location Object Browser Button Tab Property Editor Shapes Operation Object Browser Select a button item in the Buttonhole Tab. Its properties appear in the Property Editor. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor Shapes Drop-down menu on the right hand side Preset button shapes appear in the menu. Select a desired button shape. The button shape is now being replaced. All other relevant buttons are also being replaced.

Title: CREATE CUSTOM BUTTON TEXTURE: Apply Custom Button Texture
Content: Objective Apply custom button texture to buttons in Marvelous Designer. Location Property Editor Material Diffuse Map Operation Navigate to Object Browser Button Tab and select the button item to be edited. The button item's properties appear in the Property Editor. Follow the indicated guideline below: Property Editor Material Diffuse Map The file browser appears. Locate and select the custom button texture and select Open. The custom button texture is applied to the selected button item.

Title: Create Button
Content: Objective Create buttons and place them as desired. Location Main Menu Materials Button Button 3D Toolbar Button Operation Create Button Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Button 3D Toolbar Button Click on a desired point on the 3D Garment or 2D Pattern. A button is now being created at the designated location. Input Measurement for Button Position Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Button 3D Toolbar Button Right-click on the 2D Pattern where buttons would be placed. Moving Distance window appears. Input desired measurements for accurate placement. Placement preview depending on the input value displays along the mouse in the 2D window. Click OK to place. The buttons are now being created.

Title: Button List Window
Content: When creating a button, The Default Button is applied as default setting and displayed in the button list window. Once the Default Button style is modified, it lasts until rerun of the program and it is unable to be deleted.

Title: Duplicate as Buttonhole to Symmetric Pattern
Content: Objective Duplicate buttons as buttonholes, or buttonholes as buttons, to its Symmetric Pattern. Location Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Click on the button or buttonhole to be duplicated to its Symmetric Pattern. The selected button or buttonhole is highlighted in yellow. Right-click on the selected button or buttonhole. The right-click pop-up menu appears. Depending on the selected item, select Duplicate as Button to Symmetric Pattern or Duplicate as Buttonhole to Symmetric Pattern. The selected button or buttonhole is duplicated as a buttonhole or button, depending on the selected item, to its Symmetric Pattern.

Title: Copy Button Style
Content: Objective Copy and modify a button in order to create a new button style or adjust its properties. Location Object Browser Button Tab Copy Operation Object Browser Select an item in the button tab. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Button Tab Copy A new button item with the same properties of the selected item is now being created.

Title: Reset Button Style Property
Content: Objective Reset button item properties to default value (ver2.5.0). Location Object Browser Button Tab Right-Click Button Item Pop-Up Menu Reset Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Button Tab Right-Click Button Item Pop-Up Menu Reset The button item properties are now being reset back to default value.

Title: Apply Button Style
Content: Objective Apply button styles onto buttons as desired. Location Object Browser Button Tab Operation Apply Button Style In Property Editor Click on a button and select a button style in the Property Editor. The selected button style is now being applied to the button. Select A Button And Apply Button Style Select a button. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Button Tab Assigned to Selected Patterns The button style is now being applied to the selected button. Select A Button And Apply A New Button Style Select a button. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Button Tab Assigned to New Fabric A new buttonhole style is now being added to the buttonhole list window and applied at the same time.

Title: Create Additional Button Style
Content: Objective Create a new button style. Location Object Browser Button Tab Add Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser Button Tab Add A new item named after 'Button 1, 2' is now being created and applied.

Title: Create Buttonholes along Pattern Outline (ver5.1.0)
Content: Objective Create buttonholess along a Pattern Outline in a constant interval and distance. Location Main Menu Materials Button Buttonhole 3D Toolbar Buttonhole Operation Create Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu Materials Button Buttonhole 3D Toolbar Buttonhole Right click on a Pattern Outline. The Create Buttons/Buttonholes along Pattern Outline window appears. Note: To select multiple lines, press down the Shift key and click the lines to be selected. Configure below options as needed: Start Position Distance Set the distance between the buttonholes and the selected line. Interval Set the distance between the buttonholes and the Pattern Outline. Reverse The direction of which buttonholes are created is reversed to the Start Point. Replicate Interval Adjust the distance between the buttonholes. Number of Button/Buttonholes Adjust the number of buttonholes to be created. Click OK. Buttonholes are created as a group. Select Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu Materials Button Buttonhole 3D Toolbar Buttonhole Click on a buttonhole or a Pattern Outline where buttonholes are created. All buttonholes in a group are selected. Note: Click again while the group of buttonholes are selected to select a single buttonhole. Change selected buttonholes' properties or style or use right-click pop-up menu. Any changes made are applied to all buttonholes in the same group. Group information cannot be copied or duplicated. Note: Grouped buttonholes cannot be moved. Unlink Follow the indicated path below: Main Menu Materials Button Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar Select/Move Button Right click on the buttonholes or the Pattern Outline and select Unlink Buttons/Buttonholes. The link between the buttonholes are removed.

Title: 6. Sewing and Simulation
Content: In this video, we'll show you how to continue sewing your garment and learn how to use the sewing tools in Marvelous Designer.

Title: Reset Bounding Volumes (ver4.2.0)
Content: Objective Reset Bounding Volumes to the original placement after adjustments. Location Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Reset Bounding Volumes Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Avatar Avatar Editor Arrangement Bounding Volume Reset Bounding Volumes Bounding Volumes are replaced with their original placements.

Title: Apply Graphic Image
Content: Objective Place graphic images on Patterns. Use this function to express Garment details such as placed prints, embroideries, or logos. Location Main Menu Materials Graphics Graphic (2D Pattern) / Graphic (3D Pattern) 3D or 2D Toolbar Graphic.png Graphic (2D Pattern) / Graphic (3D Pattern) Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Graphics Graphic (2D Pattern) or Graphic (3D Pattern) 2D or 3D Toolbar Graphic.png Graphic (2D Pattern) or Graphic (3D Pattern) The file browser appears. Select a graphic image file and load. Click on a Pattern where the graphic image should be placed. The Add Graphic window appears. Enter the desired values for the graphic dimensions and position: Width Set the width of the graphic image. Height Set the height of the graphic image. Link or unlink the aspect ratio of the graphic image. Position Outline Set the distance from the left, right, top, or bottom of the graphic outline to the pattern outline. This menu only appears when placing the graphic in the 2D window (ver2.5.0). Center Set the distance from the center of the graphic to the left, right, top, or bottom of the pattern outline. This menu only appears when placing the graphic in the 2D window (ver2.5.0). Click OK to place the graphic image. Note: Add graphics directly by right-clicking on a thumbnail of an image file in the Library window, then select Add as Graphic from the pop-up menu (ver2.4.0). When importing an AI file with multiple artboards as a graphic, the AI/PDF window appears where artboards can be reviewed and the desired artboard can be selected (ver4.0.0).

Title: 3D File (LXO) Export
Content: Objective Export garments and avatars as LXO file format which is compatible with Modo. The LXO file format includes Geometry and Material information. Location Main Menu File Export LXO Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu File Export LXO The Save File window appears. Designate the file saving path and the file name. Then, select Save. The file is exported as a LXO file format.

Title: Select All Faces (Above ver4.2.0)
Content: Objective Select and modify all surface of an Avatar. Location Right Click on Avatar Select All Faces Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Right Click on Avatar Select All Faces All surface of the Avatar is selected.

Title: TOPSTITCH STYLE PROPERTIES: Exaggerate Topstitch
Content: Objective Express the caved line when topstitches are stitched on the real garment. Location Object Browser Topstitch Tab Topstitch (Click Topstitch Style) Property Editor 3D Operation Follow the indicated guieline: Object Browser Topstitch Tab Topstitch (Click Topstitch Style) Property Editor 3D Toggle on the 3D option. 3D shadow is added under the Topstitch to express the caved line. Use below options to adjust the caved line's Intensity or Thickness. Option Description Normal Map Select the Normal Map. Intensity (%) Adjust the caved line's intensity. Thickness Adjust the caved line's thickness.

Title: Topstitch Right-Click Pop-Up Menu
Content: Objective Edit Topstitch using the right-click pop-up menu. Location Main Menu Materials Topstitch Edit Topstitch 2D Toolbar Edit Topstitch Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Materials Topstitch Edit Topstitch 2D Toolbar Edit Topstitch Right click on the Topstitch to be edited. The right-click pop-up menu appears. Refer to below table and choose appropriate option in need. Option Name Select All With Same Property All Topstitches that have the same properties with the selected one are selected. Assign to New Topstitch A new Topstitch style is applied to the selected Topstitch. A new Topstitch style is created in the Object Browser when this option is selected. Delete Delete the selected Topstitch. Add Internal Line on Topstitch (ver4.2.0) Create an Internal Shape right on top of the selected Topstitch.

Title: TOPSTITCH PROPERTIES: Extend Topstitch
Content: Objective When the start or end point of a Topstitch does not reach or sticks out of the Pattern outline, extend it to fit to the Pattern. When using the Free Topstitch tool, the starting point is going to be the first click point. Location Topstitch Property Editor Extend Start / Extend End Operation Select a Topstitch with Edit Topstitch tool in the 2D window for changing its properties. Topstitch properties appear on the Property Editor. Follow the indicated guideline below: Topstitch Property Editor Extend Start / Extend End

Title: Show Picking Point
Content: Objective The Picking Point in Marvelous Designer refers to a blue point which appears on the 2D Pattern and the 3D Garment when you click on a Pattern on the 3D window. Show or hide the Picking Point at your convenience. Location Main Menu Display 2D Pattern Show Picking Point

Title: 7. Fabric and Finalizing
Content: In this video will guide you through the crucial steps of finishing your garment design for accurate simulation and export. Our expert tips and tricks will help you easily achieve professional results, ensuring your creations are ready to shine on any platform.

Title: Free Sewing (2D)
Content: Objective Freely establish Sewing Lines on Pattern outlines and Internal Shapes/Lines. Location Main Menu Sewing Free Sewing 2D Toolbar Free Sewing Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu Sewing Free Sewing 2D Toolbar Free Sewing Click, drag and click on Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start and end points of the first half of the seam. Similarly, click again on another Pattern outline or Internal Shape/Line to establish the start point of the second half of the seam. Drag the mouse cursor as a blue point appears guiding the length of the first half of the seam. The mouse cursor snaps to the blue guide point. Be mindful to make the Directional Notches parallel to each other and click to complete the second half of the seam. Note: The face of the Directional Notch of a Sewing Line defers depending on the order of establishing the start and the end point of the Sewing Line. Right click while establishing the Free Sewing Line to enter the desired length of the Sewing Line in the Create Sewing Line window. When establishing the second half of the seam, difference in the Sewing Line lengths appears in blue next to the mouse cursor. If the difference exceeds 1 inch, the difference appears in red to alert the user. Use the shortcut to establish M:N sewing lines. For more detail, please reference M:N Free Sewing.

Title: Smooth Avatar (ver4.2.0)
Content: Objective Smooth Avatars' surface by adjusting its Mesh count. Since the program speed may be reduced with more Avatar Mesh count, please use the feature only when its necessary. E.g.: When Avatar's Mesh appears on the tight 3D Garments, such as leggings. Location 3D Toolbar Select/Move Select Avatar Property Editor Smooth Avatar Operation Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar Select/Move Select Avatar Property Editor Smooth Avatar The Divide Mesh option is activated and its child option, Level (1-3) appears. Type in desired value between 1 and 3 to Level (1-3). Selected Avatar's Mesh is divided or merged based on the typed value. Note: Larger the Level (1-3) value is, smaller the Meshes are.
